published_statement: No single published statement: the tree cites none. The only source sentences available here, each READ by a sibling audit and restated (not re-read): Flambaum 0705.3704 p.4, 'One can only measure the variation of dimensionless quantities' and 'the measurements of the variation of the electron-to-proton mass ratio mu = m_e/M_p is equivalent to the measurements of the variation of X_e = m_e/Lambda_QCD'; Godun 1407.0164 p.4, the constraints on alpha-dot and mu-dot 'assume local position invariance and linear time variation', and optical E3/E2 transitions have mu-sensitivity B_E3 = B_E2 = 0 ('negligible'). The tree's own statement (massform.py:220-224): 'P-UNIFORM: where nothing sources it, the vev takes one value everywhere. This is a PREMISE, named. ... it is supported by the measured constancy of fermion masses, which is not read here. No owner boolean asserts it.'
published_hypotheses: Only dimensionless ratios are measured (Flambaum 0705.3704 p.4, via sibling audit): a 'constancy of fermion masses' is in fact a constancy of mu = m_p/m_e (or of alpha, g_p combinations), never of a mass or of v directly
mu tracks X_e = m_e/Lambda_QCD (Flambaum p.4, chiral limit M_p ~ 3 Lambda_QCD); a Lambda_QCD co-varying with v is not excluded by the measurement itself (Flambaum p.3-4 GUT models, 'model dependent')
Clock drift limits assume local position invariance and linear time variation (Godun 1407.0164 p.4, via sibling audit)
Every fermion-mass measurement is made where the fermion is: in labs, absorbing gas clouds, stellar atmospheres, the primordial plasma (structural, not a sentence of any read source)
Every measurement is a finite-precision bound B, not an equality (structural)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H-YUK-FIXED -- massform.py:222-223 (and :815-816, :1623-1624) moves from 'constancy of fermion masses' to 'the vev takes one value'. The measured object is a ratio (Flambaum p.4). COMPUTED (rederive B1-B3): the Jacobian of ln mu over (ln v, ln y_e, ln y_light, ln y_c, ln y_b, ln y_t, 1/alpha_s) has rank 1 and a 6-dimensional null space; d ln v = 1 with d ln y_e = K_mu = -7(1-S)/9 leaves mu EXACTLY constant. Ratio constancy implies v uniformity only if Yukawas do not co-vary. In the SM they are constants, so this is a hypothesis the SM supplies, but it is unnamed at the site.

DROPPED H-AS-FIXED / no common rescaling -- same sites. COMPUTED (B4): with Yukawas fixed, d(1/alpha_s(mu0)) = -7/(2 pi) = -1.114 per unit d ln v also keeps mu exactly constant. (C1): if Lambda_QCD moved one-for-one with v, K_mu = 0 and mu would be blind to v. The tree's own address.py:99-116 names H1/H2 for exactly this and gets K_mu = -0.73 / -0.94; massform's support sentence does not carry them.

ADDED EXTRAPOLATION (sampled matter-bearing places to unsampled unsourced places) -- massform.py:224-226: 'On P-UNIFORM the field at the seat before arrival already has the value it has wherever massive matter is measured'. A fermion mass measures phi only where the fermion is. TEMPLATE's seat is by definition a place whose Higgs-given mass is not yet present, so no fermion-mass measurement can sample it. The wording ('wherever massive matter is measured') makes the step visible and the status word is PREMISE, so this is an unnamed step inside a named premise, not an over-claim.

WEAKENED EXACTNESS -- massform.py:220 'one value everywhere' is exact, and any measurement is a bound B. COMPUTED (D1-D3): on H-YUK-FIXED with H1 or H2, |dv/v| <= B/|K_mu|, a factor of 1.30-1.42 (H1) or 1.01-1.10 (H2) over the READ S span 0.0096-0.0935. For every finite B, |eps| < 1.42 B is unexcluded at the sampled places, while TEMPLATE (C1) is refused for every r < 1. The refusal therefore does not rest on the measurement's precision. C1 also rests on D15/D16 (a lower |phi| needs a local source), which is theory, not this measurement.

CIRCULARITY RISK, recorded, not graded -- Godun p.4 (via sibling): clock mu-dot limits ASSUME local position invariance. P-UNIFORM is local position invariance of v, so a clock drift limit supports it only as far as the LPI-coupling limits, which are separate measurements, are also used. The tree names no specific measurement, so this cannot be pinned to a site. It applies if the future read uses clock data.

NO STATUS INFLATION -- massform.py:223 'not read here', :1621-1627 P_UNIFORM_STATUS = 'PREMISE', and 'No owner boolean asserts it'. The tree does not over-represent the measurement, and the drifts above are about what the measurement could establish if read, not about a claim the tree makes of it.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested as far as it can be here. The tree used NO datum for this result (massform.py:223 'not read here'), so there is no author's datum to have been outdated. The owner is the tree, and the measurement authors could not be read. The question becomes whether MORE or BETTER data could change what the measurement says about P-UNIFORM. Computed, it cannot on its own. Shrinking any bound B shrinks the unexcluded |dv/v| < 1.42 B at the SAMPLED places (D1-D3). It leaves untouched (i) the exact null directions B3/B4 (a Yukawa or high-scale alpha_s co-variation keeps mu exactly constant at any B), (ii) the common-rescaling blindness C1, and (iii) the fact that a fermion mass samples phi only where fermions already are. Precision data narrows a number, while those three are hypotheses that data of this kind cannot discharge. Evidence the other way: nothing computed or read here indicates any variation. The tree's verdicts do not rest on the measurement's value, since P_UNIFORM is a PREMISE (E1-E2), C1 also uses D15/D16, and C5 (STOCK on H-PRESENT) needs no P-UNIFORM at all (massform.py:233-236). Having the data would therefore change no D27/S10/SR5 verdict; it would change how well supported the premise is. The one datum M's lens flags as genuinely contested, early-universe m_e, concerns z ~ 1100 and is NAMED-NOT-READ here.
grade_evidence: OPEN because the external result cannot be read here. The tree cites no measurement or value, and every attempt to read the literature at source failed: alphaXiv quota exceeded on all four calls, and arXiv is refused by the proxy. By M's rule it is not flattened to STANDS. What IS checked, by sympy with ALL PASS, is the logical map from any measured ratio bound B to P-UNIFORM. That map would NARROW the support whatever B turns out to be. (1) Measurement constrains one combination of (v, Yukawas, alpha_s), since the Jacobian has rank 1 and exact null directions exist (B1-B4), so uniformity of v follows only on H-YUK-FIXED and H-AS-FIXED, which massform.py:222-223 does not name. (2) Exact uniformity is stronger than any bound (D3). (3) The measurements sample only matter-bearing places, and massform.py:224-226 extrapolates to the unsourced seat. None of this is WRONG: there is no counterexample to uniformity in nature, only to the INFERENCE from ratio constancy alone. The tree does not over-claim ('not read here', status PREMISE, no boolean asserts it). No verdict moves: VEV_IS_UNIFORM = P_UNIFORM is a premise, C1 also rests on D15/D16, and C5 needs no P-UNIFORM.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED (the expected grade once read): read the review 1009.5514 and at least one current mu-drift/LPI clock paper and one quasar/white-dwarf mu paper at source, confirm that they report ratio bounds with the hypotheses above (LPI assumption, finite precision, sampled locations), and quote their B. The computed drifts B1-B4, C1 and D1-D3 then attach to read statements. To STANDS: massform.py would name H-YUK-FIXED and H-AS-FIXED (or cite address.py's H1/H2) and the sampled-places extrapolation at the support sentence, and the read measurements would show no variation. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a READ measurement or accepted fit showing a nonzero present-epoch or local variation of mu, or of m_e, beyond its errors; an early-universe (z ~ 1100) m_e fit alone would not reach the present-day seat. To WRONG: only a READ, established nonzero variation of v at unsourced places, which nothing here indicates.
